title: 2014_PMC5779422_Human_papillomavirus_vaccination_coverage_among_adolescents_2007
ehr_evidence: CDC analyzed data from the 2007–2013 National Immunization Survey-Teen (NIS-Teen) and national postlicensure vaccine safety data among females and males.
summary: Assessment of HPV vaccination coverage among US adolescents aged 13–17 years from 2007–2013 and postlicensure safety monitoring from 2006–2014.
key_findings: Vaccination coverage with ≥1 dose increased from 53.8% (2012) to 57.3% (2013) among girls and from 20.8% (2012) to 34.6% (2013) among boys.
Receipt of ≥1 dose by age 13 increased by an average of 5.9% (95% CI = 2.8%–9.0%) with each new birth cohort, reaching 46.8% (95% CI = 41.2%–52.5%) for the 2000 cohort.
Missed vaccination opportunities ranged from 9.3% (95% CI = 8.1%–10.8%) for the 1994 cohort to 83.7% (95% CI = 77.8%–88.2%) for the 2000 cohort.
If missed opportunities were eliminated, coverage for the 2000 cohort could have reached 91.3% (95% CI = 87.9%–93.8%) by age 13.
VAERS received 25,176 adverse event reports post-HPV vaccination; 92.4% of HPV4 reports were classified as nonserious.
study_design: Cross-sectional survey analysis with birth cohort analysis and passive safety monitoring
population: Adolescents aged 13–17 years in the United States
limitations: Low cell phone household response rate (23.3%)
Missed opportunity evaluation limited to encounters with other vaccinations
VAERS passive reporting cannot determine causality
data_availability_statement: CDC, National Opinion Research Center at the University of Chicago. National Immunization Survey-Teen: a user’s guide for the 2012 public-use data file. Chicago, IL: National Opinion Research Center; 2014. Available at ftp://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/health_statistics/nchs/dataset_documentation/nis/nisteenpuf12_dug.pdf.
